features.description: Heterogeneous handler shapes can share one App.
acceptance: An executable test registers def() -> String, def(Int) -> User, and def(Request) -> Response handlers in one app and dispatches each through handle(Request) -> Response.
Registration keeps the runtime handler value syntax app.get["/users/{id}"](get_user), or compiler evidence shows why it cannot.

Storage candidates (capturing closure, trampoline, function pointer + context, compile-time generated wrapper, type erasure, compile-time handler parameter) are compared with minimal reproductions and compiler output recorded in docs/DX.md.

Runtime handler value syntax kept: handlers stored as Int address bits + same-type trampoline (one private generic _register), guarded by comptime assert size_of[F]() == size_of[Int]().

Comparison table in docs/DX.md 'Handler model (M0.5 spike)'.

features.description: Prove a real localhost HTTP round trip through Flare and Muntin.
acceptance: A real local HTTP request enters through Flare, crosses the Muntin adapter, dispatches a Muntin route, and returns the expected response.

features.description: Deliver one path parameter to a handler as Int without manual application parsing.
acceptance: The public syntax is proven to compile on the supported Mojo version and documented in docs/DX.md.
GET /users/42 yields handler input Int(42).
Invalid integer input produces documented client-error behavior.
The same handler signature works with in-memory and any enabled real backend.

Concretely: production muntin.App accepts app.get["/users/{id}"](get_user) with def get_user(id: Int) -> String, in the same App as existing def() -> String routes; the segment is converted to Int by Muntin before the handler is called, with no parsing or Request access in application code.

GET /users/abc (and other non-integer segments, including forms Mojo's Int(String) would accept such as +42, ' 42', 4_2) returns 400 'Bad Request' without invoking the handler; GET /users and paths with a different segment count or static segment return 404; a method mismatch returns 404; existing exact routes behave as in M0.
Binding is positional: a {name} segment is not checked against the handler parameter's name, and docs say so. A route whose {param} count does not match the handler fails to compile.

One App registering the typed route is driven through muntin.testing.TestClient and through a real loopback request to Flare's HttpServer serving MuntinHandler; both observe the same status and body for an integer path whose handler output differs from the raw segment (e.g. /users/042 -> '42') and for /users/abc -> 400. Routing and extraction live in Muntin; the adapter is not changed to understand {id}.

Any handler-storage mechanism is safe or, if unsafe, private, justified and contained; the choice and alternatives are recorded in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md. ./scripts/check.sh, ./scripts/test.sh, ./scripts/check_flare.sh pass locally and in CI on Ubuntu and macOS.
evidence: src/muntin/app.mojo: App.get overloaded on def() thin -> String and def(Int) thin -> String, stored as a Variant (no unsafe code); App.handle matches {name} segments and converts to Int (optional '-', ASCII digits, Int range) before calling the handler, else 400.

./scripts/test.sh -> exit 0: tests/test_app.mojo 13/13 (/users/42 -> '42', /users/042 -> '42', +42/' 42'/4_2/abc/overflow -> 400 'Bad Request', /users, /users/, /user/42, POST -> 404, exact routes unchanged, first registered match wins). ./scripts/check.sh -> exit 0: 6 tests/compile_fail fixtures rejected with their expected 'constraint failed' text (arity, malformed literal).

./scripts/check_flare.sh -> exit 0: adapters/flare/test_localhost_roundtrip.mojo 2/2; one App with /hello and /users/{id} over loopback through Flare HttpServer + unchanged MuntinHandler gives /users/42 -> 200 '42', /users/042 -> '42', /users/abc -> 400, /users -> 404, each equal to TestClient; no leftover process. CI verify + flare green on ubuntu-latest (ubuntu24) and macos-latest (macos26).
Planted mutations each turned a check red (list in AGENT_PROGRESS.md); fresh-context review found no material issue; git diff --check clean.

features.description: Separate path from query at Muntin's Request boundary and deliver one query value to a handler as Int without manual application parsing.
acceptance: Request boundary in Muntin core: Request(method, target, body) splits the request target at the first '?'; Request.path is the text before it and is the only input to route matching; Request.query is the raw text after it ('' when there is no '?'). muntin.testing.TestClient and the Flare adapter pass the raw target and do not split, parse or interpret the query themselves.

Route matching sees only the path: GET /hello?x=1 -> 200 'hello'; GET /users/42?x=1 -> 200 '42' (the path Int is unchanged, not parsed from '42?x=1'). Every M2-001 behavior without a query is unchanged, including compile-time route checks and first-registered-match-wins.

Public syntax proven to compile on Mojo 1.1.0 and documented in docs/DX.md: app.get["/items?{limit}"](list_items) with def list_items(limit: Int) -> String. The route literal names the query key because Mojo 1.1.0 cannot reflect handler parameter names; binding is positional and docs say so. The number of {..} placeholders in path plus query must equal the handler arity at compile time; a malformed query part (empty, static text, {}, a key containing '=', '&', '?', '#' or braces) fails to compile at the registration call.
GET /items?limit=10 -> 200 '10'; GET /items?limit=010 -> 200 '10' (proves Int conversion happened before the handler); unrelated keys are ignored (GET /items?other=z&limit=10 -> '10').

Query rules, documented and tested: pairs separated by '&'; key and value split at the first '='; a pair without '=' has an empty value; keys compared byte for byte, case-sensitively; no percent-decoding of keys or values; the value is converted with the same strict Int rule as path parameters. A missing key, a duplicated key, an empty value, or an invalid Int (abc, +10, ' 10', 1_0, %31%30, out of range) returns 400 'Bad Request' without invoking the handler. A path or method mismatch returns 404.

Handler storage: the closed Variant is reassessed; the value's source (path segment or query key) is route metadata, so the existing def(Int) arm is reused if possible and any new arm is justified. docs/ARCHITECTURE.md records the arm set and what would add arms next. No unsafe storage is adopted.

Parity: one App registering /hello, /users/{id} and /items?{limit} is driven through TestClient and through real loopback requests to Flare's HttpServer serving the unchanged MuntinHandler; both give the same status and body for /hello?x=1, /users/42?x=1, /items?limit=010 ('10'), /items (400), /items?limit=abc (400) and a non-matching path with a query (404). The adapter contains no query parsing and does not use Flare's query helpers.
./scripts/check.sh, ./scripts/test.sh, ./scripts/check_flare.sh and git diff --check pass locally, and CI verify + flare pass on Ubuntu and macOS.
evidence: src/muntin/http.mojo: Request(method, target, body) splits at the first '?' into path and raw query; TestClient and the unchanged Flare adapter pass the raw target. src/muntin/app.mojo: app.get["/items?{limit}"](list_items) reuses the def(Int) Variant arm (no new arm, no unsafe code); _query_value + _parse_int run before the handler, else 400.

features.description: Migrate production handler storage from the closed Variant to the M2-003 typed box, behavior-preserving, with no new handler shape.
acceptance: Production App no longer stores handlers in Variant[def() thin -> String, def(Int) thin -> String]; the M2-003 typed box with pointer erasure, or a strictly smaller equivalent, is the only production handler storage, and App.handle has no per-shape branch.

Public API unchanged: app.get[route](handler) syntax, Request/Response, App.handle(Request) -> Response; exactly the non-raising () -> String and (Int) -> String handlers are accepted; no new extraction, return-conversion or raising-handler API, and the box type is not exported or in any public signature.

The erased value is a pointer to storage allocated for the handler type F, never reinterpreted function-value bits; the pointer and its invoke/drop functions are produced together from the same F by the internal constructor, and a mismatched trampoline fails to compile (executable fixture).

Each stored handler has one owner; moving App or its route list keeps every route working and each allocation is freed exactly once, shown by an ownership oracle on the production storage type and an App move test with both shapes. Copy/clone support is removed unless a production need is shown.
Unsafe operations live in one internal module with a documented MutUntrackedOrigin invariant, and a canonical check fails if they appear elsewhere in src/muntin or if the module is exported.

Route matching, query extraction, 400/404 behavior, all tests/compile_fail fixtures, test_app, the spikes, the adapter tests and the real Flare loopback parity test are unchanged and green; planted ownership/pairing mutations turn checks red.

./scripts/check.sh, ./scripts/test.sh, ./scripts/check_flare.sh and git diff --check pass locally, CI verify + flare pass on Ubuntu and macOS, and a fresh-context review finds no unresolved material issue.
evidence: src/muntin/_handler_storage.mojo (private, not exported): move-only _Erased whose only field is a ThinAllocation[_Header]; the header holds the erased OwnedPointer[F] pointer with _unsafe_invoke_box/_unsafe_drop_box instantiated for the same F; no clone/copy. app.mojo: the two App.get overloads box the handler with _call_none/_call_int; App.handle makes one invoke; no Variant. scripts/check_unsafe.sh (in check.sh) confines unsafe operations, box fields and helper imports to that module.

features.description: Decide Muntin's argument-extraction contract (which request source fills each handler parameter, and how a raw value becomes application type T) before request-body extraction, with Mojo 1.1.0 compiler evidence; production handler shapes and storage unchanged.
acceptance: Source binding and typed conversion are decided separately. Source-binding alternatives compared: positional remainder becomes the body, explicit registration metadata, parameter wrapper types (Body[T]/Path[T]/Query[T]), and type-directed binding; conversion alternatives compared: a Muntin-owned conversion trait (source-specific vs source-neutral), a user-supplied decoder at registration, a static-factory convention without a trait, and reflection-based construction. Each is tested or eliminated with a pinned-compiler result or a stated DX reason.

The viable direction is proven across a module boundary: an application module defines a move-only CreateUser and handlers (CreateUser) -> String and, as evidence only, (Int, CreateUser) -> String; a separate library-side spike module converts and dispatches them through the production _Erased box without naming CreateUser, without new unsafe code and without changing src/muntin/_handler_storage.mojo.

Builtin versus application-defined types, body ownership against the current owned-String Request, the one-body rule, compile-time diagnostics, and the extraction-failure (400) versus future handler-failure boundary are each decided with executable evidence or an explicit limitation.

Production supports exactly def() -> String and def(Int) -> String, as after M2-004; no public extraction/body/decoder trait, app.post, raising handler or new overload enters src/muntin. Retained probes and must-not-compile fixtures run under check.sh/test.sh.

docs/ARCHITECTURE.md has an 'Argument extraction decision' section (alternatives, evidence, chosen source-binding and conversion contracts, builtin treatment, error boundary, storage interaction, revisit conditions); DX.md labels body syntax as target; AGENT_PROGRESS.md records PR #10 merged and the next smallest body slice.

features.description: First typed request-body slice decided by M2-005: body-only POST with one application-defined FromBody parameter, converted by Muntin before the handler.
acceptance: Public syntax compiles on Mojo 1.1.0 and is documented in docs/DX.md: from muntin import App, FromBody; struct CreateUser(FromBody) with @staticmethod def from_body(body: String) raises -> Self; def create_user(body: CreateUser) -> String; app.post["/users"](create_user). FromBody is a public Muntin trait refining Deinitable & Movable; conversion uses the M2-005 mechanism (generic B: Movable & Deinitable refined by comptime assert conforms_to(B, FromBody), Int rejected by type equality), with no downcast, rebind_var or __extension.

Production adds only body-only POST: one required FromBody parameter (borrowed or var), a route literal with zero path and query placeholders, and a non-raising handler compatible with def(var B) thin -> String. -> String is the canonical documented shape; Mojo 1.1.0 also accepts implicitly String-convertible returns such as StaticString, matching App.get since M2-001. Int, String and Request bodies, (Int, B) and other multi-parameter shapes, body handlers on GET, raising handlers, -> Response and other return types that do not convert to String, raw Request handlers, JSON, and optional or multiple bodies remain unsupported.

Body conversion happens in Muntin (App.handle and its adapter) before the handler: a valid body reaches the handler as the converted value; from_body raising returns 400 'Bad Request' without invoking the handler; no matching method and path returns 404. The body comes from Request.body only, never from the path or query, and Request.body is not consumed.
The application body type is defined outside src/muntin, may be move-only (not Copyable), and Muntin never names it; mojo precompile src/muntin builds the package without any application module.
src/muntin/_handler_storage.mojo is unchanged and the unsafe surface is not expanded: no new unsafe operation, and no body or request logic in the storage module (scripts/check_unsafe.sh guards it).
muntin.testing.TestClient.post(target, body) builds Request("POST", target, body) and calls App.handle, with no conversion logic.

Flare remains transport-only (adapters/flare/muntin_flare.mojo unchanged). One App registration gives the same status and body through TestClient and through real loopback requests to Flare's HttpServer serving MuntinHandler for a valid body, an invalid body, a wrong method and a missing route.

Must-not-compile fixtures, checked by scripts/check.sh, protect the boundary: missing FromBody conformance, Int body, a path or a query placeholder on the body-only overload, and unsupported multi-parameter, raising, return-type, raw-Request and GET-body shapes.
Existing GET/path/query behavior, tests and diagnostics remain green and unchanged.

Retained tests and planted mutations catch skipped conversion, handler invocation after conversion failure, the wrong body source, accidental route-value or body acceptance, backend-side conversion, and storage/unsafe expansion.
docs/DX.md, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/SPEC.md, feature_list.json and AGENT_PROGRESS.md record only facts that became production reality; no CI run IDs or commit SHAs in committed docs.
A fresh-context skeptical review finds no unresolved material API, ownership, extraction/error-boundary, backend-leakage or scope issue.

features.description: Decide how an application-defined handler result R becomes a Response (typed handler return conversion) with Mojo 1.1.0 compiler evidence, keeping the registration syntax and the M2-004 _Erased storage; production behavior unchanged.
acceptance: Candidates compared with pinned-compiler results or a stated DX reason: a Muntin-owned conversion trait on application types, an explicit converter at registration, static/convention-based conversion without a trait, and a direct Response special case.

The chosen contract is proven across a module boundary: application return types live in an application module, the library-side spike never names them (built without the application module), and mixed String-compatible and application-defined-return handlers coexist in production _Erased, unchanged, for GET and POST.

The decision states how R becomes Response; the mechanism; whether conversion moves or borrows R, with move-only evidence; how -> String and String-compatible returns (StaticString) are treated, distinguishing the declared return type from compatibility with the registered function type; whether -> Response is a direct escape hatch; whether conversion may raise, without designing the application-error model; and one return policy across GET and POST independent of argument extraction.

Production supports exactly the M2-006 handler shapes: no typed-return overload, exported response trait, -> User, -> Response, raising handler, (Int, B), JSON, headers, middleware or new unsafe code; _handler_storage.mojo unchanged. The only src/muntin change is FromBody's docstring: from_body(body: String) is the current public body-conversion input contract and future body capabilities are additive.

docs/ARCHITECTURE.md has a 'Typed response decision (M2-007)' section recording the contract, String/StaticString treatment, the Response decision, ownership and error semantics, rejected alternatives with evidence, reconsideration conditions and the exact next production slice; DX.md section 5 labels the shape as decided but not production.

features.description: Make the M2-007 typed-response contract production behavior: public ToResponse, Response conforming, one R: ToResponse overload beside each existing String overload.
acceptance: muntin exports trait ToResponse(Deinitable, Movable) with non-raising def to_response(var self) -> Response; Muntin Response conforms and returns itself by move, so -> Response is a direct escape hatch with no Response-specific registration overload.

Every existing String overload keeps its exact signature, checks and messages; -> String remains canonical and String-compatible returns such as -> StaticString resolve through the existing String overloads, not the generic ToResponse path.

_call_none, _call_int and _call_body are generic over the result R and a compile-time response policy (_text / _converted[R]); exactly one R: ToResponse overload is added beside each argument shape: GET def() -> R, GET def(Int) -> R, POST def(B: FromBody) -> R, with the same route-literal and body validation as its String twin.

Executable production evidence: an application-defined move-only User: ToResponse returned from no-arg GET, Int path GET, Int query GET and body-only POST; -> Response preserves the chosen status and body; -> StaticString keeps String behavior; the conversion runs exactly once after a successful handler call; 400/404 run neither handler nor conversion; App moves preserve mixed String/ToResponse handlers; result types live outside src/muntin and Muntin never names them.
TestClient and real loopback through Flare's HttpServer serving MuntinHandler agree for at least one -> User-style route and one -> Response route.

_handler_storage.mojo byte-identical, no new unsafe code, adapters/flare/muntin_flare.mojo unchanged. Not added: raising handlers or conversions, (Int, B), raw Request handlers (the recorded var Request overload issue stays open), JSON, headers, content negotiation, middleware/state, new HTTP methods.

Must-not-compile fixtures match the new surface: fixtures that rejected -> Response become positive tests; diagnostics change only where the added overloads change compiler output; a non-conforming result is rejected at registration with a note naming ToResponse; unrelated compile-fail coverage is not weakened.

Planted mutations (conversion skipped, Response status lost, StaticString routed through generic conversion, conversion on 400/404, extraction changed, generic overload without its trait bound, storage/unsafe expansion) turn checks red; a fresh-context review finds no unresolved material issue; ./scripts/check.sh, ./scripts/test.sh, ./scripts/check_flare.sh and git diff --check pass locally, and CI verify + flare pass on Ubuntu and macOS.

features.description: Production POST handler with exactly one Int route value followed by one typed FromBody body, returning String or R: ToResponse, using the M2-005 extraction contract and the M2-008 response contract.
acceptance: Exactly two App.post overloads are added: def(Int, var B) thin -> String and def(Int, var B) thin -> R with R: ToResponse; B is an application-defined, possibly move-only FromBody type; the route value comes from exactly one path placeholder or one query placeholder with the existing Int rules; binding is positional (route value, then body), never by parameter name.

One adapter reuses the existing extraction and response policies: route value converted first, then the body, then the handler once, then _text or _converted[R] once. No match is 404 with no extraction, conversion or handler; an invalid matched path value, or a missing, duplicated, empty or invalid query value, is 400 before body conversion (a missing path segment does not match the route and is 404); a body conversion failure is 400 before the handler; no fallthrough after a matched route fails.

Executable evidence covers path and query sources and both return policies, with a move-only body and a move-only typed result; TestClient and real loopback through Flare agree for a valid path value + body, a valid query value + body, an invalid value, an invalid body and one ToResponse result.

Unsupported shapes stay closed at compile time: missing route value, too many route values (incl. path + query), a body type without FromBody, Int in the body slot, reversed (B, Int), two bodies, a raising handler, a result that is neither String-compatible nor ToResponse. Existing diagnostics are preserved where overload resolution does not inherently change.

_handler_storage.mojo and adapters/flare/muntin_flare.mojo unchanged, no new unsafe code; _call_none, _call_int and _call_body unchanged. Not added: several route values, path + query values together, two or optional bodies, String/builtin bodies, raising handlers or conversions, raw Request handlers, JSON, headers, new methods, middleware, state.

Planted mutations (ordering, source binding, handler after a conversion failure, swapped argument order, skipped response conversion, guards removed, storage/unsafe expansion) turn checks red; a fresh-context review finds no unresolved material issue; ./scripts/check.sh, ./scripts/test.sh, ./scripts/check_flare.sh and git diff --check pass locally, and CI verify + flare pass on Ubuntu and macOS.
